title: Meet Go
story: Chilaka found a small, fast language from Google. Go programs are compiled and strict. That strictness is a gift: the compiler catches mistakes for you.
goal: Read how a Go program starts, then fill in two small gaps.

tests.label: Finish every try-it and quick check

hints: Read each block, then do the TRY IT and QUICK CHECK parts.
Every interactive block must be done to finish the lesson.
Take your time. Nothing here is timed.
socratic: Compare your result with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the most useful thing you learned here?

blocks.text:
Every Go program lives in a **package**. A program you can run uses `package main` and a function called `main`.

To print, you import the `fmt` package and call `fmt.Println`.

blocks.title: The smallest Go program

blocks.text: Notice there are no semicolons, and strings use double quotes. Go also refuses to compile if you import something and never use it.

blocks.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program prints `Hello, Aata-gram`.
blocks.why: fmt is the formatting package, and Println prints a line.

blocks.q: Which line makes a Go file a program you can run?
blocks.why: A runnable program is `package main` with a `main` function.
